competences: The learner identifies key facts about citizenship.
The learner explains information about Ways of becoming a citizen of Uganda using reference texts.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, spells, reads and writes citizenship, citizen, registration.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify facts about citizenship.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to answer the available sourced questions about Ways of becoming a citizen of Uganda.
priorKnowledge: Learners have already studied Uganda and related Social Studies concepts. They build on this earlier work to learn about citizenship.
materials: Primary Five SST reference on Ways of becoming a citizen of Uganda
references: P.5 Social Studies Lesson Notes Term III: Uganda as an Independent Nation

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls the previous SST topic and introduces citizenship. They ask "Who is a good citizen?" and listen to learners' first responses before referring to the source notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall previously studied content and answer the opening question, explaining their ideas in short sentences.

steps.stage: Development: Meaning and key facts about citizenship
steps.content: Acquisition of Uganda citizenship by fraud.( illegally ) Good citizenship Single citizenship. This is the legal right of belonging to one particular country. Dual citizenship. This is the legal right of belonging to more than one country. Loss of citizenship of Uganda. If one’s citizenship was acquired unlawfully/ by fraud. By denouncing the citizenship. Responsibilities/duties/obligations of a citizen Citizenship by registration Citizenship by Naturalization Citizenship by descent Citizenship by birth
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about citizenship on the chalkboard, including "Acquisition of Uganda citizenship by fraud.( illegally ) Good citizenship; Single citizenship. This is the legal right of belonging to one particular country.". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Features and related facts about citizenship
steps.content: Refers to a strong love one has for one’s country. A patriotic citizen is a person who has or shows great love for his / her country. Through descent (is the legal right of belonging to a country a person gets when his / her ancestors were citizens in that country) A Passport is an official document issued to citizens allowing them to travel abroad and enter the home country. A National ID card is a legal document given to all Ugandan citizens for easy identification. A National ID shows national identity and also enables citizens to get access to the social services provided in the country. By descent Conditions under which a person can lose citizenship By forging Ugandan citizenship A person married to a Uganda citizen for at least a period of three years. This is where a person from another country is made a citizen of a specified country after spending many years (20years)

steps.content: To protect the citizens and their property through the army. To provide social services like education to the citizens. A person born by parents who are Ugandans becomes a citizen of Uganda by birth. Citizenship by adoption Citizenship by foundling A foundling is an abandoned child of unknown parents and is found in Uganda. steps.content: Who is a good citizen? | Define dual citizenship | How some one can lose citizenship of Uganda? | How can one lose his chance of being a citizen of Uganda? | State any four responsibilities of a good citizen in Uganda.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher gives the original questions, starting with "Who is a good citizen?" and "Define dual citizenship". They monitor pupils as they answer, check responses against the source material and provide corrections.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the sourced exercise questions independently, consult their copied notes and correct any mistakes after marking.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews the factual content on citizenship, asks "Who is a good citizen?" and follows up with "Define dual citizenship". They confirm the answers and assign the remaining sourced practice.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners state one important fact from their lesson notes, answer the final oral questions and correct their written work.

assessment: Use the original questions "Who is a good citizen?" and "Define dual citizenship", along with other listed items, to assess learners' understanding and correct errors from the source material.
homework: Answer the remaining sourced question, including "How one can become a citizen of Uganda?"
